mechanism_narrative: The current Federal Funds Rate of 3.94% is below the 5-year average of 4.2%, indicating a relatively accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in the current snapshot despite FEDFUNDS being below 4.2%, or historical Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0% in a 3-month window, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where UNRATE rises above 5.0% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is below 4.0% and CPIAUCSL is above 210.0, it indicates a policy error where monetary policy is too loose while inflation is accelerating, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0% and remaining above for at least 6 months), the S&P 500 tends to underperform, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or historical Rank IC < 0.03 over 5-year rolling window.

failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS < 50k and UNRATE > 5.0%, or interaction effect p > 0.05 over 5-year rolling window.
